notes.headline: Everpure (formerly Pure Storage): revenue up 51% on AI and hyperscaler demand; full-year guidance raised for the third time
notes.takeaway: Revenue rose 51% to $1.5 billion, product sales 77%, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.86 beat the $0.78 consensus. Everpure raised its fiscal 2027 revenue forecast to $5.20–$5.21 billion, 42% growth, and its operating-income forecast by about 14%, after winning a design deal with a second top-five hyperscaler. The shares rose 3.6%.
results: Everpure, the storage company formerly known as Pure Storage, reported revenue of $1.5 billion for the quarter ended November 1, up 51%. Product revenue rose 77% to $948 million and subscription services revenue rose 19% to $512 million. Subscription annual recurring revenue reached $2.2 billion, up 20%, and remaining performance obligations — contracted future revenue — $4.2 billion, up 44%.

Non-GAAP gross margin was 69.2% and non-GAAP operating income $345 million, a 23.6% margin; GAAP operating income was $150 million. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.86 against $0.58 a year earlier. Operating cash flow was $443 million and free cash flow $265 million, with $1.1 billion of cash and investments.
The company bought back 0.5 million shares for about $67 million. It joined the S&P 500 in September and was again named a leader in Gartner’s enterprise storage rankings.
mgmt: Chairman and chief executive Charles Giancarlo said the results reinforce Everpure’s role as the trusted partner for critical data infrastructure as organisations modernise their data estates. Chief financial officer Tarek Robbiati said revenue and operating income exceeded the top of guidance, with growth in the core business and core AI offerings complemented by new businesses, and that the company is raising full-year guidance for the third consecutive quarter while reiterating its preliminary fiscal 2028 outlook.

Everpure now expects fiscal 2027 revenue of $5.20–$5.21 billion, up from $5.03–$5.07 billion, and non-GAAP operating income of $1.08–$1.09 billion, up from $940–$960 million. For the fourth quarter it guided to revenue of $1.50–$1.52 billion, up 42% to 43%. It also announced a design win with a second top-five hyperscaler for its DirectFlash technology.
view: For most of its history Pure Storage was a premium seller of flash storage arrays to corporate data centres, growing in the low teens. The rename to Everpure coincides with a different company: one growing above 40% because the largest cloud providers have started using its DirectFlash technology to replace hard drives in their own data centres. Meta was the first top-five hyperscaler; a second design win this quarter turns a single big contract into a pattern, and that is what drove product revenue up 77%.

The quality of growth is strong. Margins near 69% at a time of rising flash-memory prices show pricing power, operating income is growing much faster than revenue, and the $4.2 billion of contracted future revenue gives visibility. Raising guidance three times in one year while reiterating next year’s outlook is a sign of a management team that set conservative targets and is now consistently beating them.

The risks sit in the same place as the opportunity. Hyperscaler deals are large, lumpy and negotiated hard, so they can depress margins and make growth uneven quarter to quarter, and customers of that size can always build their own solutions. The surge in NAND flash prices that has helped Sandisk and Micron also raises Everpure’s input costs. At about 31 times this year’s non-GAAP earnings (and more than 100 times GAAP earnings), investors are paying for the hyperscaler business to become a durable second engine; this quarter is the strongest evidence yet that it can.
notes.watch: Watch the size and timing of shipments to the two hyperscalers, gross margin as flash prices rise, subscription ARR growth in the core enterprise business, and the formal fiscal 2028 guidance in February.
